title: Production of the BCH Aggregator
bodyHtml:
To produce the Aggregator, we integrated exomes from the Children’s Rare Disease Cohort (CRDC) together with other exomes contributed by BCH investigators. The exomes were sequenced from samples ascertained according to various criteria. Phenotypes were assigned to each sample by mapping information in their Electronic Health Records and/or ascertainment criteria to one of 24 high-level terms from the Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO). Within the resource, samples are grouped primarily by their HPO term(s) and secondarily by their “cohort”, defined uniquely by the contributing investigator and IRB protocol used for their collection. The data page provides information about the specific cohorts, ascertainment criteria, and HPO terms used within the resource.

Data Generation

CRDC exomes were sequenced via heterogeneous protocols, with a consistently applied consenting framework described in https://www.nature.com/articles/s41525-020-0137-0. Other exomes were sequenced through more heterogeneous protocols, information about which is not available for all samples (quality control was performed to control for heterogeneous sequencing technologies). Initial read alignment and variant calling was performed with the hardware-accelerated DRAGEN platform using reference genome hg38. Samples were then jointly called following GATK best-practices.

Quality control

After joint calling, samples were subjected to a previously published quality control procedure. Ancestry was inferred for each sample by calculating principal components of common variants and comparing these to 1000G project samples. A variety of ancestry-adjusted quality control metrics were then calculated for each sample (e.g. number of alternate alleles, mean allele balance, number of singletons), and outlier samples according to one metric, or a collection of metrics, were excluded from downstream analysis. Sample relatedness was also calculated from common variants.

View a summary of the quality control procedure.

Phenotype analysis

Following quality control, each HPO term was analyzed in succession. For each term, the number of variant carriers (heterozygous and homozygous) was calculated. These variant counts are shown on the gene page and variant pages.

In addition, for each HPO term burden tests were conducted for each gene following a previously published procedure. Variants were annotated by the Variant Effect Predictor and 16 bioinformatic prediction algorithms in the dbNSFP plugin. These annotations were used to define 7 “masks”, or variant filters – these masks were nested and range from severe (LofTee mask, predicted loss-of-function) to likely deleterious (5/5, five different bioinformatic algorithms classify the variant as damaging) to all missense variants (0/5 1%, all nonsynonymous variants with frequency < 1%). Association analyses were then conducted by collapsing variants within each mask as a “burden” score and regressing this score against a “case” label – cases were defined as individuals with the HPO term, and controls were defined as all other samples. Burden results are shown on the gene page.
